shots.say: What is inside a camel's hump?
And why does baby Sandy have no hump at all?
I'm Milo. Let's find out together!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we fly far away, to the hot, sunny desert.
Here we are! Look at all that sand.
The desert is hot in the day. Phew!
This is Sandy. Sandy is a baby camel.
A baby camel is called a calf. Can you say calf?
And this is Sandy's mama. Hello, Mama!
Mama is tall. Sandy is small.
When Sandy was born, she stood up fast.
In just half an hour, she could walk beside her mama!
Step, step, step! Off they go.
Sandy stays close to her mama.
Mama and Sandy hum to each other.
Mmm, mmm, mmm.
Mmm, mmm, mmm.
Can you hum like a camel?
Mmm, mmm, mmm!
Now look at Mama's back. She has a big, tall hump!
But Sandy has no hump. Just a little tuft of curly hair.
Sandy looks up at Mama's hump. What is in there?
What do you think? Is it water? Or is it fat?
It is fat! A camel's hump is full of fat.
Not water. No, no, no!
The fat is like a lunch box.
It gives the camel energy when there is no food around.
One big hump can hold eighty pounds of fat!
Let's say it together. Fat, not water!
Mama and Sandy walk down the rocky trail.
Look! A thorny bush. Those thorns are sharp.
But camels have tough lips. Mama can eat thorny plants!
Munch, munch, munch. Can you munch like Mama?
Sandy has a little snack too. Nibble, nibble.
When a camel eats a lot, her hump stands up tall.
When there is no food for a long time, she uses the fat.
Then the hump gets soft, and leans over. Flop!
A tall hump is full. A floppy hump is empty.
Mama just had a big lunch. Is her hump tall, or floppy?
Tall! Mama's hump is full of fat.
Now they find a pool of cool water. Splash!
Camels do not keep water in the hump. They drink it!
A thirsty camel can drink thirty gallons of water,
in only thirteen minutes! Gulp, gulp, gulp.
After that, a camel can go a week or more without a drink.
Drink up, little Sandy!
Let's count Sandy's sips. One, two, three!
Ahh! That feels good.
Whoosh! The wind is blowing the sand around.
Sand in the air tickles my eyes!
But camels are ready for a sandy day.
They have two rows of long eyelashes.
The eyelashes keep sand out of their eyes. Blink, blink!
Can you blink like a camel? Blink, blink, blink!
And look at this nose. A camel can close its nose!
Open. Closed. Open. Closed! No sand gets in.
Camels have big, wide feet too.
Each foot spreads out when it steps down.
That helps them walk on soft sand. Step, step, step!
No sinking for Sandy!
Far, far away, it is cold and snowy.
Sandy's cousins live here. Look closely at this camel's back!
One hump, two humps! This camel has two.
Some camels have one hump. Some camels have two.
Long eyelashes keep out the snow and ice, too.
How many humps does Sandy's mama have? One, or two?
One! Mama has one big hump.
The sun goes down. Time to remember what we learned!
What is inside a camel's hump? Water, or fat?
Fat! It is the camel's lunch box.
Was baby Sandy born with a hump? Yes, or no?
No! Just a little curly tuft.
How do camels keep sand out of their eyes?
With two rows of long eyelashes!
As Sandy grows up, her hump will grow too.
One day, Sandy will have a hump just like Mama's.
And it will be full of... fat! You remembered!
Today we learned three big things.
One. A hump is full of fat, not water.
Two. A baby camel has no hump yet.
Three. A camel can close its nose!
Mama hums a sleepy song for Sandy.
Mmm, mmm, mmm. Mmm, mmm, mmm.
Good night, Sandy. Good night, Mama.
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
